screens.prompt: In B8, work out Friday's cost as the crates in B6 times the rate in C7, with the rate address locked so a fill keeps it on C7.

hints.syntax: ROUND takes the arithmetic and the digits: =ROUND(B6*$C$7,2).
hints.func-round: Money gets rounded to two places, and ROUND is the function that does it in the same cell as the arithmetic.
hints.require-ref: Read the crates from B6 and the rate from C7; a typed 110 stops matching the sheet.
hints.value: 110 crates at 1.15 each is 126.5. Check that the rate you multiplied by is the one in C7.
hints.error: Dividing the cost by zero returns #DIV/0!, which is what C8 produces if you point the rate there.

reject.why: the closing bracket is missing, so nothing computes
the arithmetic is right but the cost is not rounded, and the screen is practising ROUND
the rate cell is one row too low, so the cost is zero
the rate cell is empty, so the cost comes back as zero
the crates typed into the formula, so the row no longer follows the sheet
a cost divided by zero returns #DIV/0!
adds the crates to the rate instead of multiplying, and without rounding

docs.explain: B6 holds 110 crates and C7 holds the rate per crate, 1.15. Friday's cost is B6 times C7, rounded to two places so the column carries no fractions of a penny. The dollar signs are the point of the drill. A plain C7 filled down becomes C8, then C9, and the cost column quietly multiplies by blank cells. Writing $C$7 locks the column and the row, so a copy down keeps pointing at the rate. C$7 would also survive a fill down, which is why it is accepted here, but it would break across columns. A bare C7 means 'the cell one column to the right of me, wherever I end up'. Dragging the formula down walks the rate off its row and changes the cost in every row below.

errors.text: The cost was divided by an empty cell, usually a rate column that is filled in later.
The formula was copied from a cell that sits beside the rate, so a relative C7 walked off the sheet and the reference broke.

docs.atWork: A rate card with one price per unit at the top, copied down a hundred order lines.
docs.outcome: Lock the cell a formula must keep reading when it is filled down.
docs.dataset: Crates by day at one rate

seo.title: Excel absolute references: lock a cell
seo.description: $C$7 keeps the rate fixed when the formula is filled down, while a bare C7 walks off its row and multiplies by blank cells. ROUND trims the pennies.
